whenToUse: The same actions repeat for every object, such as files, messages, or table rows.
You add fast shortcuts for experienced users.
The screen is a canvas or editor where buttons are hard to lay out.
whenNotToUse: It's the only way to do that action (right-click is easy to miss).
It sits over links or body text, where the browser's own right-click menu is more useful.
It's a main action that newcomers must know about.

alternatives.name: Dropdown Menu
alternatives.reason: Offering the same actions from a visible button.

alternatives.name: Bottom Sheet
alternatives.reason: Showing large choices after a long press on mobile.

accessibility: With the object focused, Shift+F10 or the menu key also opens it, so it works without a mouse.
On touch, a half-second long press opens it, and the first item gets focus.
Use role="menu" and role="menuitem" with ↑↓, Home, and End; closing with Esc or Tab returns focus to the object.
Offer the same actions through another button or menu on screen, so people who don't know about right-click can use them.
